title: Low-Cost FDM Fabrication of an Age-Scaled Pediatric Upper-Limb Osteology TLM Kit: Slicer Infill Ablation and Build-Orientation Validation
description: Abstract: Tactile, anatomically accurate osteology Teaching-Learning Materials (TLM) improve spatial understanding in community health training and school science classrooms, yet commercial pediatric bone models are rarely accessible in rural educational settings. We present an open-source, parametric Blender 5.2 CAD pipeline and Fused Deposition Modeling (FDM) fabrication protocol for a 5-bone human upper-limb osteology kit (Scapula, Clavicle, Humerus, Ulna, and Radius) scaled across adult (1:2, 1:1) and pediatric (5-year, 190 mm humerus; 8-9-year, 240 mm humerus) norms, incorporating modeled 2.4 mm wire-articulation tunnels for classroom assembly. Fabricating curved organic bones on high-speed desktop CoreXY printers (Creality K1, 0.4 mm nozzle) introduces two practical failure modes: (1) default slicer vertical-shell rules convert sloped bone interiors into dense internal solid infill, inflating material and print time, and (2) tilted single-piece builds (tilt40) suffer mid-print bed detachment due to minimal humeral-head contact (<4 mm2) and a tall lever arm (163.69 mm). Across 17 audited G-code jobs (poster, 1:2, and 1:1 scales), disabling ensure_vertical_shell_thickness and detect_narrow_internal_solid_infill constrained internal solid infill to 1.0%-3.8% (mean 2.31%) while maintaining 55.62% mean sparse infill without altering natural rounded geometry. Comparing three build orientations for the 240 mm Age 8-9 Humerus, zero-support split halves with 1.85 mm filament alignment pegs (split-pin) and Variable Layer Height eliminated bed-detachment failures observed in tilt40 and underside support scarring from flat tree supports. All CAD scripts, watertight STLs, .3mf plates, OrcaSlicer 2.5.1 presets, and G-code audit datasets are openly archived for community makerspaces and educators. Ideation & TLM pedagogical design by Dr. Preethi L Xavier (Physician & Independent TLM Designer); CAD & FDM fabrication by Dhamodaran KKP (Ideapattrai - Makerspace, Aarvam Learning Lab) for Payir Health Initiatives (Payir Trust) TLM.
